nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern
Illinois...
Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and
ditches may be clogged with leaf debris increasing the risk of
flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 530 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the Turkey
Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above bankfull.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City, Merrillville, South Shore,
East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart, Lansing, Crown Point,
Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith, Dyer, South Deering, St.
John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of the Four Seasons, Whiting,
Winfield and New Chicago.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
nearbyCountiesFullText.instruction:
A Flood Advisory means minor flooding along waterways and other poor
drainage areas is imminent or may already be occurring. Persons in
the advisory area should use caution and avoid flood waters.

discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 140731
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
231 AM EST Sat Nov 14 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered lake effect rain showers, possibly mixed with some
  snow, are expected to shift across far northwest Indiana and
  southwest Lower Michigan this morning. Any snow is expected to
  be limited to trace amounts.

- Scattered rain showers later this morning will diminish this 
  afternoon with mostly cloudy skies expected.

- Below normal temperatures continue today through the weekend
  followed by slowly moderating temperatures into the low to mid
  60s by the end of the upcoming work week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 230 AM EST Sat Nov 14 2026

Lake effect precipitation continues this morning across northwest 
Indiana. A larger scale upper level trough is sinking southward 
across the southern Great Lakes early this morning and southward 
passage of this upper trough should begin to create more favorable 
backing wind profiles to support eastward movement of lake effect 
precip. Along with these more favorable trajectories is 
diminishing RH in the snow production layer, which appears to be
resulting in an increased cellular nature in the regional radar
mosaic presentation. A weak mid level trough accompanying this 
upper level short wave should bring a narrow west-east axis of 
better mid level RH for a brief time in the 08Z-12Z time period 
this morning. However, this will still be a very marginal mid 
level moisture profile in the snow production layer and will be 
transitory in nature as the weak mid level trough axis sinks 
south. 

In terms of thermal profiles, sharp cooling has occurred outside of 
lake effect clouds, but as favored lake effect precip area shifts 
eastward over next several hours, sfc/near sfc wet bulbs will begin 
to creep up downwind of Lake Michigan leading to a possible 
preference to light lake effect rain showers, or perhaps even a 
little bit of drizzle at times as morning progresses as the DGZ
dries out even more behind the aforementioned mid level trough 
axis. Forecast thinking has not changed much since the last 
cycle, with any snow likely of the trace variety given the above
factors. Liquid equivalent precip will also not be in the same
ballpark as experienced past 24 hours across extreme NW Indiana 
with this lake effect precip as synoptic forcing and moisture 
depths become more marginal this morning.

Some increase in clouds is expected across the area this morning 
given this subtle backing wind profile with generally mostly 
cloudy to partly sunny skies today as narrow layer of low level 
moisture may be trapped by weak subsidence inversion. Thermal 
profiles are not significantly different from yesterday which 
should yield similar highs in the mid to upper 40s.

For tonight, a lagging weak mid/upper level short wave is forecast 
to round the departing larger scale negative upper height anomaly 
into the southern Great Lakes. Mid level moisture recovery 
looks limited however, but could see some weak rejuvenation of 
some light lake effect rain showers/sprinkles this evening. Will
maintain lows in the upper 20s to mid 30s tonight with 
expectation that low clouds should tend to linger.

The longwave pattern through the weekend should be a stable one and 
slowly evolving  in a CONUS trough-ridge-trough setup, with a cut 
off upper low across the southern Plains. This stable wave pattern 
will be accompanied by weak baroclinicity and weak advective 
trends which will make the moderation in temperatures quite a 
slow process, especially considering low level mixing will 
remain weak through early next week. There is a greater 
potential of better insolation into Sunday and Monday however, 
which will likely push highs into the lower 50s.

The extended periods of the forecast still look rather benign as 
guidance continues to suggest next Pacific wave attempts to 
dampen the upper ridge across the area for the middle of the 
week. This system looks to be quite progressive with an axis of 
better 925-800 mb mixing ratios shifting into the area late 
Wednesday. Any elevated instability along this axis looks to be 
quite limited in nature and expectation is still that better 
rain chances will be confined north of the area. 

Mid/upper level heights recover quickly behind this short wave for 
Thursday and Friday, with a potential of a larger scale and more 
dynamic eastern Pacific upper trough moving across western CONUS by 
late Thursday into Friday. A large part of central/eastern CONUS 
will experience well above normal temps downstream of this feature 
for the Thu-Sat period. Still some expected discrepancies noted
in medium range deterministic/ensemble solutions in timing of 
this feature toward the Days 6-7 period, but blended PoPs 
including low chances by next weekend still appear reasonable as
a low level jet axis and better moisture transport shift east 
into the local area.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 1243 AM EST Sat Nov 14 2026

VFR to MVFR conditions expected at the terminals, with KSBN
potentially seeing lake effect rain/snow showers (more likely
rain) as a band moves from over the Chicago area into NW IN/SW 
Lower MI during the morning/early afternoon hours. There are
questions regarding the exact arrival time, though around 15z
appears to be the best shot for MVFR ceilings. A trough to the
north shifting south into the KFWA area late this morning
(currently ceilings of 1500-2500 ft) will lead to more
persistent borderline MVFR/VFR conditions at the terminal. This
may also reach KSBN, however the western edge of the clouds
appears to be more diffuse (and will also be arriving when lake
effect band may arrive towards 15z).

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 10 PM EST this evening for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 140515

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1115 PM CST Fri Nov 13 2026

   Valid 141200Z - 151200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are unlikely across the U.S. today and tonight.

   ...Texas...

   An upper trough will develop eastward from the Southwest to southern
   Plains today. As this occurs, a 500 mb jet streak around 50-60 kt
   will overspread western/central and southern TX. The left exit
   region of the upper jet will coincide with a weak surface low
   traversing northeast NM into the TX South Plains.
   South/southeasterly low-level flow will transport modest boundary
   layer moisture northward across central TX toward the South Plains
   (mainly 50s F dewpoints) beneath cool temperatures aloft. Given cool
   thermodynamic profiles, as surface temperatures also will remain
   generally cool, instability will remain weak (500 J/kg MLCAPE or
   less). While vertical shear could support some organized storm
   structures, a lack of great buoyancy is expected to limit overall
   severe potential across TX. However, given cool temperatures aloft
   and the bulk of instability occurring between 850-500 mb within
   otherwise favorable shear, small hail could occur from portions of
   the TX Panhandle/South Plains toward central TX from late afternoon
   into tonight.

   ..Leitman/Chalmers.. 11/14/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 140657

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1257 AM CST Sat Nov 14 2026

   Valid 151200Z - 161200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE TEXAS
   COASTAL PLAIN...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms are possible across central
   and south Texas.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough over the southern Plains will continue southeastward
   and deamplify as upper ridging builds over the Midwest. A weak
   surface low will move from the southern TX Panhandle into central TX
   as surface high pressure builds to the north. To the west, a second,
   broader trough will intensify as it moves onshore over the West
   Coast. Onshore flow will favor only modest moisture transport inland
   with weak buoyancy expected. Showers and a few thunderstorms are
   possible from northern CA to WA state. Severe storms are not
   expected.

   ...Central and Southern TX...
   Early morning showers and residual thunderstorms are likely to be
   ongoing near the surface low and along the Red River vicinity. A
   surface front will begin to move southward as high pressure builds
   to the north. Broad-scale ascent attendant to the wave and strong
   low-level warm advection over the front will support modest buoyancy
   for a few hours. While some small hail appears possible with this
   early activity, instability is forecast to become increasingly
   scant/shallow with time over southern OK and North TX.

   Farther south, more robust inland moisture return and some heating
   will contribute to weak to moderate destabilization across south TX
   and the middle TX Coast. Continued low-level warm air advection
   ahead of the advancing upper trough should allow for scattered
   thunderstorms to develop by midday. Effective shear of 40-50 kt will
   likely support some more organized elements with a mix of
   semi-discrete cells and clusters. Hail and damaging gusts are
   possible with the stronger storms. While not overly robust, forecast
   soundings show modest turning in the lowest 1-2 km of the wind
   profile. Given the low-level shear and the upper 60s F surface
   dewpoints, a brief tornado is possible.

   The warm sector is forecast to become increasingly narrow into the
   evening as the cold front from the north accelerates southward. This
   will favor undercutting and some potential for upscale growth as
   storms approach the coast. Elevated buoyancy may linger behind the
   effective front into the overnight hours with a low-end risk for
   hail with the remaining storms.

   ..Lyons.. 11/14/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 140825

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0225 AM CST Sat Nov 14 2026

   Valid 161200Z - 171200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are not forecast over the US Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Mid-level ridging is forecast to strengthen considerably over the
   central US Monday as troughing deepens along the CA coast. The
   shortwave trough over the Gulf is forecast to weaken as it meanders
   eastward underneath the building ridge over the central CONUS. At
   the surface, a cold front will continue offshore through the Gulf.
   In its wake, an expansive area of high pressure centered over the OH
   Valley will intensify to 1035-1038 mb. The increasingly strong
   surface pressure gradient will reinforce offshore flow over much of
   the US, limiting available surface moisture. As a result, cool, dry
   and stable conditions are forecast for much of the country with
   thunderstorm potential likely remaining offshore.

   ..Lyons.. 11/14/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
